title: Single-use items by-law and Drill Hall future
subtitle: Also: 2023 audited financial statements, asset management plan, Elliott trustee appointment and a closed-session transit bargaining update.
overview: Council approved phase 2 of the Single-Use Items strategy and passed the related by-law, with changes. Coffee cup sleeves are no longer covered by the by-law, and businesses must accept a customer's reusable drink cup for in-store orders, except at drive-throughs or for delivery. A proposed requirement for reusable food containers was dropped for now. Staff will instead do more engagement and research with restaurants and report back. Phase 2 takes effect March 1, 2025.

On the Drill Hall, council chose not to pursue a sale for now. Staff will use up to $25,000 from the unspent 2024 Community Investment Strategy account for a city-led feasibility study and community engagement process on arts and culture uses. The City keeps ownership and keeps funding the building's structure and primary systems, and staff report back by March 31, 2025. Council also approved the 2023 audited financial statements, which staff said were expected to receive a clean audit opinion, and the 2024 Asset Management Plan.

After the closed session, the mayor reported that staff received direction on the Amalgamated Transit Union Local 1189 bargaining mandate. Council received information on the Southgate Business Park lands term sheet and gave no direction. Council also appointed a new trustee to the Elliott board.

decisions.detail: Council approved the Single-Use Items By-law as amended, removing sleeves from the accessory foodware definition and requiring businesses to accept reusable drink cups for in-store orders, except at drive-throughs or for delivery {{vote:m11}}.
Council approved the phase 2 recommendations of the Single-Use Items Reduction Strategy {{vote:m8}}.
Staff will conduct more engagement and research on reusable containers and report back to Council, without drafting a by-law requirement yet {{vote:m14}}.
Council allocated up to $25,000 for a city-led feasibility study and engagement on arts and culture uses, kept City ownership of the building, and set a report-back by March 31, 2025 {{vote:m15}}.
Council approved the 2023 Consolidated Financial Statements and the external audit findings report {{vote:m6}}.

Council approved the 2024 Asset Management Plan with baseline levels of service, to be submitted to the province by July 1, 2024, with staff to report on the timeline to sustainable funding through the 2025 budget.
Council appointed Lise Betteridge to the Elliott Board of Trustees for a term ending June 2027 {{vote:m2}}.

debate: On reusable containers, staff said restaurant representatives raised concerns about allergens, hand washing, contamination, inconsistent container sizes, extra staff time and existing labour shortages. Staff said engagement might end up in the same place.

Some councillors wanted to keep exploring mandatory reusable containers, citing landfill waste and Banff's positive anecdotal experience. Others said they could not support language that implied a by-law, and favoured encouraging and educating businesses.

The reusable container motion was narrowed to engagement and research only, so a by-law would be decided after the report back. Staff said the earlier engagement had focused on beverage containers, so this was not duplication.

Delegates on the Drill Hall supported arts use but said the process excluded equity-deserving and Indigenous groups. They objected to a $10,000 grant going to one group that applicants had not known about, and asked for an open, community-engaged process.

One councillor was concerned that keeping the building could pre-empt a later sale. Staff and the clerk said the clause only covers the period until the March 2025 report back, and Council could still decide to sell then without a reconsideration vote.
